title: Collateral, Margin and Procyclicality
summary: How initial and variation margin and collateral policies protect the infrastructure, the trade-off between prudence and procyclicality, and how to calibrate and communicate margin to participants.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How initial and variation margin and collateral policies protect the infrastructure, the trade-off between prudence and procyclicality, and how to calibrate and communicate margin to participants.
Learning Objectives: Calibrate initial margin models, look-back periods and confidence levels
Set eligible collateral, haircuts and concentration limits
Manage procyclicality and the transparency of margin calls in stress
Syllabus: Initial and variation margin: purpose, methods and calibration
Collateral eligibility, haircuts, concentration limits and reuse
Anti-procyclicality tools and margin transparency for participants
Lessons from margin spikes in commodity and bond market stress
Intended Audience: Board members, risk and audit committee members and senior executives of trading venues, CCPs, CSDs, payment systems and trade repositories
Chief risk officers, heads of compliance, internal audit and risk, treasury, default management and operations staff
Regulatory affairs, legal and strategy teams preparing for supervisory assessments or new services
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of trading, clearing, settlement or payment systems is helpful. No prior study of the PFMI is required.
Core Reading: CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012)
FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
IOSCO, Regulatory Issues Raised by Changes in Market Structure (2013)
FSB, Effective Practices for Cyber Incident Response and Recovery (2020)
